input: Pitch a mentorship program idea to HR

gold.taskTitle: Pitch a Mentorship Program Idea to HR
gold.taskDescription: The user wants to propose a mentorship program concept to their HR department and needs a clear, convincing pitch.

questions.title: What is the core purpose of this mentorship program?
questions.description: Understand the primary goal — e.g., onboarding new hires, developing leadership, supporting underrepresented groups, or boosting retention.

questions.title: Who is the intended audience for the program?
questions.description: Clarify who the mentees and mentors would be — e.g., junior employees, specific departments, all staff, or a particular demographic.

questions.title: Do you already have a concept, or starting from scratch?
questions.description: Find out if the user has a rough idea, a full proposal draft, or needs to build the concept from the ground up.

questions.title: What format will the pitch take?
questions.description: Determine the delivery method — e.g., a live presentation, a written proposal document, a short email, or a meeting conversation.

questions.title: When is the pitch scheduled or due?
questions.description: Establish the deadline or target date so the plan can be scoped and prioritized accordingly.

questions.title: What has HR's stance been on similar initiatives before?
questions.description: Learn whether HR is likely to be receptive, skeptical, or neutral, and whether past proposals have succeeded or failed.

questions.title: What outcome do you want from this pitch?
questions.description: Clarify the desired result — e.g., formal approval, budget allocation, a follow-up meeting, or just initial buy-in.
